replay_semantics: session: one locals dict per dialogue, a fresh copy of process_model_output.py's globals per exec, the cache reset per dialogue
eligibility: 1. The user turn has a gold Filled_Plan (a whitespace-only plan counts).
2. Under session replay no gold plan of its dialogue raises, up to and including this turn, on user and assistant rows alike.

3. Session replay and upstream's file-wide replay (one locals dict per file, dialogues in groupby('ID') order, i.e. Python <= 3.12) give identical pre-turn summaries, post-turn summaries and errors on every row of the dialogue up to and including this turn. Summaries compare as str() of the dict, key order included.
selection: 1. Domain quotas: total // 9 each; the total % 9 domains with the lowest _unit_hash('42:quota:{split}:{domain}') get one more.

2. Template allocation: the templates of the domain's T1 split with at least one eligible turn get quota // n_templates each; the quota % n_templates with the lowest _unit_hash('42:alloc:{split}:{domain}:{ID}') get one more.
3. Items: a template's eligible turns ranked by _unit_hash('42:item:{id}'), taken in order, skipping any turn whose dialogue already has an item, until the allocation is met.
Hash keys use this repo's split name (train, val, test) and unpadded integers; _unit_hash is skillpng.benchmarks.base._unit_hash.
digest_rule: sha256 of the sorted ids joined by newlines, first 16 hex characters
notes: This is a split manifest, not the T1 payload. Materialize the items from
the dialogue CSVs of capitalone/T1 at source_revision; an item is one
user turn of one dialogue, keyed (domain, T1 split, file, ID, turn),
where ID is a template id repeated once per file and turn counts the
dialogue's non-empty user rows from 0. Train, val and test are drawn
from T1's train, validation and test splits respectively, which are
template- and city-disjoint, so nothing crosses a T1 boundary. Every
item comes from a different dialogue. plan_digest is the sha256 of the
gold Filled_Plan and cache_digest the sha256 of the pre-turn cache
summary string, both cut to 16 hex characters; the adapter refuses an
item whose data or replay no longer gives them. Test template 26 of
flighthotelrestaurant has no eligible turn: its second user turn calls
search_nearest(hotels=hotels) before hotels exists, which only runs
upstream because a same-named variable leaks in from another dialogue
the file. Three train items (flight template 47, turn 2) have a of
whitespace-only gold plan: their target is an empty <CODE> block.
